title: [repo:objectui] Inline-edit grid: Enter neither commits nor moves to the next row, Tab does not move, and single-click can open the editor unfocused (keystrokes lost, cell commits as 0)
body:
## Summary

In the list view's inline-edit grid, **Enter does not commit the cell and does not move to the next row**; the editor simply stays open until the user clicks elsewhere. Tab does not move to the next cell either. For the "fill one numeric column down a list" task (a KPI reporter typing actual values for N indicator rows) this means every row costs a mouse click plus, if the user presses Enter expecting Excel behaviour, a confused moment. Single-click sometimes opens the editor without focusing the input, so the first keystrokes are lost and the cell commits as `0` (observed twice out of six cells in a scripted run; a double-click + select-all always works).

## Reproduction

Platform 17.2.0 console, any grid with `inlineEdit: true` and a numeric column.

1. Click a numeric cell → editor opens.
2. Type `85`, press Enter → the editor remains open with `85` in it; no "N 行已修改" bar until focus leaves the cell.
3. Press Tab → nothing moves.
4. Click another cell → the previous one commits (row marked modified), the new one opens.

Variant: single-click a cell and start typing immediately (within ~1 s) → the digits are not captured; the cell later commits as `0.0000`.

## Expected (spreadsheet conventions, which is what an inline grid promises)

- Enter commits and moves focus to the same column in the next row; Shift+Enter moves up; Tab / Shift+Tab move right / left; Esc cancels.
- The editor input must be focused (and its content selected) the moment the editor opens, so typing on single-click never loses keystrokes.
- Optional: an explicit "fill-down" affordance is not needed — Enter-to-next-row covers the KPI case.

## Environment

`@objectstack/console` 17.2.0 · `objectstack dev` · Chromium 1440×900 · zh-CN. App: objectstack-ai/kpi (`kpi_entry_line` list, column `actual_value`).
